model.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 9576) to establish the National Fraud Enforcement Division of the Department of Justice; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 10326) to enhance information-sharing capabilities between Federal law enforcement and State agencies to detect, investigate, and prosecute fraud in certain Federal programs, and to protect individual privacy; providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 210) providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to ''California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision''; providing for consideration of the joint resolution (H.J. Res. 213) providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the ''California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision''; and providing for consideration of the Senate amendments to the bill (H.R. 5334) to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes.

summary.text: The resolution would set the terms for House debate and votes on five separate legislative measures: two bills to combat fraud in federal programs (one creating a new Justice Department division and another improving information-sharing between federal and state law enforcement), two resolutions to block Environmental Protection Agency pollution rules for California vessels and harbor equipment, and a bill to extend tax deductions to early childhood educators.

hidden.labelText: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On ordering the previous question Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: 214 - 208 (Roll no. 299). (consideration: CR H5654-5655)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H5654-5656)

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on H. Res. 1530, the Chair put the question on ordering the previous question and by voice vote, announced that the ayes had prevailed. Mr. McGovern demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with one hour of debate on H. Res. 1530.
Considered as privileged matter. (consideration: CR H5646-5651)

The resolution provides for consideration of H.R. 9576, H.R. 10326, H.J.Res. 210, and H.J.Res. 213 under a closed rule with one hour of debate and one motion to recommit on each measure. The resolution provides for a motion to concur in the Senate amendments to H.R. 5334.
